method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited locator address was checked to begin an instruction of the decoded function, and the operands, name literals, vftable cells, RTTI names, jump table entries, constants and call targets named in the claims were compared with those listings by a second pass. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site and chunk counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Script argument counts, constants and calling function names come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of thirteen native registrations of the CharaBase, NpcBase, WorldMaster and Math classes: _getAllGroup, _createVirtualItem, _getNetStatUser, _printDebugLog, _getSubStatBreakage, _preloadItemSpreadSheetContainer, _getNetStatSystem, _isAccessibleInServer, _randomFloat, _getGear, _releaseItemSpreadSheetContainer, _loadWord and _unloadWord. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish group membership, item identity, status bit meaning, log routing, word table content, random sequences or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/chara_desktop_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers, the world object chain and the yield request. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. No callback has a rel32 caller.

framework.holdersNote: Each invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback.

typeRegistry.note: Entries 0 to 9 are recorded in manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json. The constructor stores the vftables of entries 10 to 13 after them. The push slot of an operator is the dword at vftable +0x08.

listBuilders.0x0072B660: three ints. Entry 0 is registry entry 0 and the entries 1 and 2 come from 0x007270B0, which selects the same entry
listBuilders.0x0073D5A0: Utf8String then three ints. Entry 0 is registry entry 3, entry 1 is registry entry 0 and the entries 2 and 3 come from 0x007271F0, which selects registry entry 0
listBuilders.note: Each builder selects registry entries through 0x00CCA210 by position, as recorded in manifests/work_binder_native_call_contract.json.

argumentReaders.0x005819A0: int, cell tag 0. A mismatched tag reaches 0x00CCA730.
argumentReaders.0x00581AE0: Bounds-tests an index against the cell vector and reads an int.
argumentReaders.0x0071CE70: Utf8String, cell tag 3. A mismatched tag reaches 0x00CCA730.
argumentReaders.note: A position beyond the Lua top is filled with one tag 6 placeholder by the marshaller 0x00D19A20, which starts at native-frame index 2.

returnPushers.0x00748870: bool, built as a tag 2 value through 0x00583E30 and appended through 0x00584EE0
returnPushers.0x00CFA1D0: LuaControlArray push slot, consumes a tag 0 count cell and that many tag 4 control cells into one Lua table, and pushes nil for a first cell of tag 6

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R], Y = [X +0x04], W = [Y] and V = [W], the chain of manifests/global_native_call_contract.json.

fields.Y +0xE4: Pointer to the object whose first dword is the group registry. _getAllGroup and the _getGroup helper of manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json read it.
fields.Y +0x12C: Object that _createVirtualItem passes to 0x0076B4C0 together with the Lua thread.
fields.V +0x660: Log sink pointer that 0x004D6D90 tests before it calls 0x004CE760. Recorded in manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json.
fields.V +0x664: Object whose virtual slots 9 and 10 receive the word path from _loadWord and _unloadWord.
fields.V +0x8BC: Object that 0x0056D990 and 0x0056D9F0 search by path against the static array at 0x01338158.
fields.V +0x174F8: Sheet manager pointer that 0x004D74C0 returns. Recorded in manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json.

worldObject.tier: STATIC for the offsets and calls, INFERRED for the roles.

yieldRequest.note: ECX is the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08 and the argument is the checker pointer, as recorded for _wait in manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json.

callers._preloadItemSpreadSheetContainer: 0x006F2913 with s_PreloadResumeChecker, vftable 0x00FD6150, with no first test

framework.invalidParameterRoute: A failed cell vector size test calls 0x009D22B4. The target cursor contract records that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.

arguments.handlerRead: 0x00581AE0 tag 0, read only when the cell tag is 0
arguments.note: Optional filter. A tag 6 cell, which the marshaller supplies for an omitted argument, selects the lookup without a filter.

returns.pusher: 0x00584F70 for the count, then 0x00748B30 once per control, joined by push slot 0x00CFA1D0
returns.note: One Lua table of GroupBase controls. An empty result is an empty table.

rows.behavior: Resolves the group registry at the world object, collects the group handles of the receiver identity and pushes one GroupBase control per handle as a Lua table. A tag 6 first cell lists every group of the identity. A tag 0 first cell lists only the groups whose record dword at +0x04 equals the int. Any other tag lists nothing. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback loads the ExecuteParameters pointer, pushes the flag 0 and calls the helper 0x00701250 with a stack temporary as ecx. The helper stores ecx, forwards it as the this of 0x006E2240 and never reads it, so the receiver pointer of the callback is not used. The lookups key on the identity at ExecuteParameters +0x0C.

The helper takes the world chain R from 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04, X from the dword at R, Y from the dword at X +0x04 and the dword at Y +0xE4. The thunks 0x006C5840 and 0x006C5850 load the dword at that address as the group registry. The same Y +0xE4 object serves the _getGroup helper recorded in the nameplate and group contract.

An empty cell vector reaches 0x009D22B4. Otherwise the tag byte of cell 0 selects the lookup. Tag 6 calls 0x006C5840 with the identity address ExecuteParameters +0x0C and the result vector. Tag 0 reads the int through 0x00581AE0 and calls 0x006C5850 with the identity address, the int address and the result vector. Any other tag calls nothing and leaves the vector empty.

0x006C46F0 and 0x006C47B0 reserve the result vector to the count at registry +0x1C through 0x006D4860, with 0x10 byte elements. They walk the list headed by the registry dword at +0x18 and call 0x006C3B30 on the group record at node +0x18 with the registry and the identity address. A nonzero result appends an element built from the dwords at node +0x10, +0x14 and +0x18. 0x006C47B0 first compares the dword at group record +0x04 with the int and skips the node on a mismatch.

The count is the byte distance of the result vector divided by 0x10, or 0 for a null start, and is pushed first through 0x00584F70 to the return container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C. Each element then goes through 0x006E2240, which creates a control through 0x00CC80A0, casts it to GroupBase and copies 16 bytes of the element to control +0x68, and the control is pushed through 0x00748B30. The creation recipe is the one of the _getGroup record in the nameplate and group contract. This callback passes the flag 0.

The return list builder 0x0072B870 declares one entry of registry entry 10. The type registry constructor 0x00CC9D60 stores the StackOperator vftable 0x0110E0C8 for entry 10, whose RTTI name is LuaControlArray. Its push slot 0x00CFA1D0 reads a count cell of tag 0 and then that many cells of tag 4 and builds one Lua table with the indexes 1 to count. A first cell of tag 6 pushes nil instead.

The shipped scripts contain 10 call sites in 4 chunks. The chunks are chara/charabaseclass, chara/npc/populace/populacelinkshellmanager, chara/player/playerbaseclass and commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

Three sites pass no argument, six pass one argument and one passes an argument list that ends in a call or vararg. Three of the one argument sites, two in the linkshell manager and one in the debugger chunk, pass the constant 20002. This comes from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan of the installed scripts with tools/decode_lpb.py. No tracked artifact carries argument counts, constants or calling function names.
The int is a group kind filter and the result is the list of groups that the identity belongs to. These roles come from the native name and the comparison with the record dword at +0x04.
The registry contents, the writers of the group records, the meaning of the constant 20002, the test in 0x006C3B30 and the element layout that 0x006D5F80 appends were not traced.

rows.behavior: Reads three ints and finds or creates the item package record under the key in the dword at 0x00FE0508 in the item package manager of the receiver. It allocates a client item object, builds a CreateClientItemResumeChecker and tests it once. A completed checker pushes the control at checker +0x18. Otherwise the native moves the checker to a heap copy and requests a yield with it.

facts.claim: The callback builds the inert helper 0x006DD450, calls the body 0x00702A20 with the ExecuteParameters pointer, the receiver and the flag 0, and destroys the helper through 0x006DD4D0. The body never reads its ecx.

The body reads cell 0 as an int. For cell 1 it tests the vector size, then the tag byte. Tag 6 stores the value 1 and any other tag reads an int. Cell 2 is read as an int with a vector size test and no tag 6 branch. A short vector reaches 0x009D22B4.

The package key is the dword at 0x00FE0508, which holds 0xFF in the file. The item package manager is the object that 0x006F51A0 returns for the receiver, the lazy +0xD8 manager of the item package record in the chara and desktop contract. 0x006E5BA0 searches it for the key. When the search returns 0 the body allocates 0x24 bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs a package record with 0x006EF0D0 and registers it through 0x006F19D0.

The body calls 0x00758E00 on the dword at Y +0x128 and 0x0076B4C0 on the dword at Y +0x12C with that result and the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08. It then allocates 0xD0 bytes and constructs the client item object with 0x006EF490.

0x006E0440 constructs the resume checker. It stores the vftable 0x00FD5958, whose RTTI name is CreateClientItemResumeChecker, over the base vftable 0x00FD4F5C. It builds a 0x10 byte member at checker +0x08, stores its first four arguments at +0x0C, +0x10, +0x14 and +0x1C and its byte argument at +0x20, and clears the dword at +0x18 and the byte at +0x21.

0x006F6A80 runs on the checker with the world handle. When the byte at checker +0x21 is 0 it calls 0x006E2D30 on the dword at checker +0x08, stores the result in the byte, calls 0x006E2770 with the world handle and stores the result at checker +0x18. It returns 1 only when the byte is 1 and 0x006ED9E0 on the dword at checker +0x0C returns 1. A return of 1 pushes the dword at checker +0x18 as a control through 0x00748B30.

A return of 0 calls 0x006E0550, which allocates 0x24 bytes, default constructs a CreateClientItemResumeChecker there with 0x006DF2F0, moves the fields of the local checker into it and clears the moved local fields. The native then calls the yield request 0x00CD2860 with the Lua thread at ExecuteParameters +0x08 and the heap checker, and pushes nothing in this body.

The argument list builder 0x0072B660 declares three entries. Entry 0 is registry entry 0 (int) and entries 1 and 2 come from 0x007270B0, which selects the same entry. The return list builder is 0x0072C260, one LuaControl*.

A fresh record therefore holds 0 at +0x10.
The shift count is the cl register, so the processor masks it to 5 bits. An index of 25 reads bit 0 and an index whose sum with 7 reaches 32 wraps. No range test exists, so any int returns a bool.

arguments.note: Kind from 1 to 8. Any other value pushes false.

returns.note: True when bit 8 minus kind of the chara status dword is 1.

rows.behavior: Reads one int kind, resolves the chara of the receiver identity and tests one bit of the dword at chara +0xF8. Kind 1 tests bit 7 and kind 8 tests bit 0. A kind outside 1 to 8 pushes false. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as an int, copies the identity at ExecuteParameters +0x0C to a stack dword and takes W from the world chain. It passes the identity address to 0x0075C1D0 on W, which searches the identity registry at V +0x4AC through 0x004D9970 and returns the dword at +0xF8 of the found chara through 0x00585410.

The kind minus 1 indexes the jump table at 0x006FA0D4 when it is 7 or below as an unsigned compare. Its eight cells select a right shift of 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 and 0 for the kinds 1 to 8. The result is the low bit after the shift. Any other kind leaves the value 0 and pushes false. No instruction raises an error for an out of range kind.

No instruction tests the registry result before the load at +0xF8, so the run time result for an identity that is absent from the registry is unknown. The same holds for _isActorMainStatMode in the chara and desktop contract.

rows.behavior: Reads two floats lo and hi, advances the 32 bit state dword at Math +0x64 with the linear step of _randomInteger, takes r from bits 16 to 30 of the new state and pushes lo plus r over 32768 times hi minus lo, clamped to lo from below and held under hi. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds the inert helper 0x0078BEB0 on the stack, calls the body 0x0078D130 with the ExecuteParameters pointer and the address of receiver +0x64, and destroys the helper through 0x0078BEC0.
The body tests the cell vector size and reads cell 0 and cell 1 through the float reader 0x0071BAC0, each with its own size test.

The state step is state times 0x41C64E6D plus 0x3039 stored back to the dword, then an arithmetic shift right by 16 and a mask with 0x7FFF. This is the generator of _randomInteger in the binding map contract.

The value r is converted with FILD and multiplied by the double 3.0517578125e-05 at 0x00FE0568, which is 2 to the power -15, and stored as a 32 bit float. The span hi minus lo is formed in double precision. The result is the float of lo plus that product, formed by a double multiply and add through the x87 stack.

When lo is greater than the sum, the result is lo. When the sum is not below hi, the result is lo plus the span times the double 0.999969482421875 at 0x00FE0580, which is 32767 over 32768. Otherwise the sum stands. The result is pushed through the float pusher 0x007489D0.

The argument list builder 0x0072C310 declares two entries and both use registry entry 1 (float). The return list builder 0x0072B390 declares one entry of registry entry 1. The holder 0x00726F60 is the Math non-const wrapper with the type descriptor 0x012C09E8.

The shipped scripts contain 3 call sites in 2 chunks. The chunks are commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev and commanddebugger/commanddebuggergm. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.

Every site passes two arguments. The first is the constant 0 and the second is the result of a multiplication. Scripts reach the native through the global math as math:_randomFloat(0, x). This comes from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan of the installed scripts with tools/decode_lpb.py. No tracked artifact carries argument counts, constants or calling function names.

The initial value and the other writers of the state dword at Math +0x64 and the result for lo above hi were not run. The ordering of the clamps comes from the compare instructions and was not exercised.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument and no result. It resolves the five item sheet controls by name and, for each value in the vector at receiver +0x138, tests every sheet with the value and calls the sheet routine 0x006F63A0 for a positive test. It then empties the vector. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds the five Utf8String literals itemDataSheet at 0x00FD4C78, equipmentSheet at 0x00FD4C88, weaponSheet at 0x00FD4C98, armorSheet at 0x00FD4CA4 and accessorySheet at 0x00FD4CB0, resolves each through 0x00CC7A20 and casts it to the SpreadSheet type descriptor 0x012C2308, as _preloadItemSpreadSheetContainer does.

The vector is the begin and end pair at receiver +0x138 and +0x13C, behind the proxy dword at +0x134. For each value the callback walks the five sheet controls, calls 0x006DFFC0 on the sheet with the value and, on a nonzero result, calls 0x006F63A0 on the sheet with the world handle ExecuteParameters +0x04 and the value. 0x006F63A0 works on the list at sheet +0xB8 and the container at sheet +0xC4 with the value.
After the walk the callback erases the whole range of the vector at receiver +0x138 by setting the end pointer to the begin pointer.
Both list builders are the empty builder 0x0072B440. The holder 0x0072D4B0 is the NpcBase non-const wrapper.

rows.behavior: Reads a name and an int, forms the path xtx/ plus the name and hands path and int to the word table object, which loads the table whose record name matches. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as a Utf8String through 0x0071CE70 and cell 1 as an int through 0x005819A0 with a second size test. The argument list builder is 0x0072BD30 (Utf8String, int) and the return list builder is the empty builder 0x0072B440.

It takes W as the dword at Y of the world chain. It builds a Utf8String from the literal at 0x00FD4E28, which is xtx/, and calls 0x0044AB90 with a result string, that prefix and the name. The routine calls 0x00447200 on a temporary with its second argument, 0x004488F0 on the temporary with its third argument and 0x00447200 again to fill the first.
0x00447200 copies a string and 0x004488F0 appends one, so the result string is the prefix followed by the name. These routine roles come from the call shape and were not read.

The callback calls 0x0075CD00 on W with the result string and the int. The routine loads V, takes the object at V +0x8BC through 0x004D7520 and calls 0x0056D990 with the string and the int. It then takes the object at V +0x664 through 0x004D74F0 and calls its virtual slot 9 (offset 0x24) with the same two values.

0x0056D990 compares the string through 0x00445D20 with the three Utf8String records of the static array that starts at 0x01338158 with stride 0x54 and ends at 0x01338254. For a match whose pointer at object +0x60 plus 4 times the index is nonzero it calls 0x00CA71A0 with the int. A string with no match returns false and does nothing else.
The holder 0x00726CA0 is the WorldMaster const wrapper with the type descriptor 0x012C1328. The callback does not read its receiver.

ledgerCandidates.note: These are the Lua names of the unimplemented ledger rows that this record gives a registration, an argument list, a return list and a callback contract. A client that implements _getAllGroup needs the group registry behind Y +0xE4. A client that implements _createVirtualItem needs the item package manager, the client item object and the CreateClientItemResumeChecker poll. A client that implements the status bit rows needs the status record at CharaBase +0xDC and the dword at chara +0xF8. A client that implements the spreadsheet container rows needs the sheet manager behind V +0x174F8 and the s_PreloadResumeChecker poll. A client that implements the word rows needs the table array at 0x01338158. _randomFloat needs the state dword at Math +0x64.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order of the framework.

Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time. An argumentCounts key open marks a call whose argument list ends in a call or vararg expression.
The Lua bytecode facts come from the installed client scripts. Their sources are not redistributed, and the tracked script metadata holds names and line numbers only.

_getSubStatBreakage, _getGear and the registry lookups of the status rows dereference the chara that 0x004D9970 returns without a test, so their run-time effect for an identity that is absent from the registry is unknown.

_createVirtualItem and _preloadItemSpreadSheetContainer end in a yield request. The poll that the yield request makes, the completion of each checker and the value that a resumed script receives were not traced.
The invalid-parameter route ends in a process terminate on the evidence of the target cursor contract. The calls that reach it with an empty cell vector were not run.

manifests/status_effect_findings.json places the breakage bits in a status dword of the CharaBase +0xDC substruct, while the _getSubStatBreakage callback reads the dword at +0xF8 of the chara that the identity registry at V +0x4AC returns. The relationship between the two locations was not traced.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish group kinds, item ids, status bit meaning, sheet names, word table names, log routing or server behavior.

The selection of the natives is by static script names in xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json and the switchboard orders. It is not an execution trace and not a census of the natives that a script reaches on a given path.

The script argument counts, constants and calling function names come from a local bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries. They are INFERRED. Only the call-site and chunk counts are MEASURED against napi_index.json.
